item.content:encoded:
After opening their final road trip of the season with a 4-2 loss to the Rangers, the Red Sox will look to get back on track when the teams meet again Wednesday.
The Sox didn’t get much help from Patrick Sandoval in Tuesday’s opener. The lefthander allowed four runs in a 44-pitch second inning and lasted just 2⅔ innings.
They could benefit from a deep outing from Jake Bennett, who gets the nod as the Sox look to inch closer to clinching a postseason berth with their magic number at five.
The Rangers will counter with lefthander MacKenzie Gore.
Here is a preview.
Lineups
RED SOX (82-69): Anthony LF, Jones DH, Abreu RF, Contreras 1B, Rutschman C, Durbin 3B, Story SS, Kiner-Falefa 2B, Eaton CF
Pitching: LHP Jake Bennett (9-7, 3.69 ERA)
RANGERS (75-76): Foscue 2B, Seager SS, Jung 3B, Burger 1B, Nimmo RF, Langford LF, Duran CF, Diaz DH, Jansen C
Pitching: LHP MacKenzie Gore (8-11, 4.62 ERA)
Time: 8:05 p.m.
TV, radio: NESN, WEEI-FM 93.7
Red Sox vs. Gore: Willson Contreras 9-16, Jarren Duran 0-3, Jahmai Jones 2-4, Isiah Kiner-Falefa 1-2, Andruw Monasterio 0-1, Adley Rutschman 3-8, Trevor Story 0-2, Connor Wong 0-3
Rangers vs. Bennett: Has not faced any Texas batters
Stat of the day: The Red Sox have won 24 of their last 35 road games, and are 40-23 away from Fenway Park since April 25.
Notes: Bennett is coming off his worst start of the season after allowing six runs in 5⅓ innings of a 6-4 loss to the Angels. … Over their last 10 games, Red Sox relievers have allowed five runs in 33 innings. … The Sox are 7-7 against the Rangers since Aug. 12, 2024. … They are 22-14 against lefthanders, and 14-15 against the AL West. … Gore’s 31 starts are the most in the majors. He is 0-1 with a 1.46 ERA and 16 strikeouts in two starts against the Red Sox.

item.content:encoded:
Romy Gonzalez seemed like a staple of the Boston Red Sox's offensive attack plan just a year ago. Now, with the playoffs looming, it's become difficult to see where he fits into the picture.
Having been demoted to Triple-A on Aug. 4, Gonzalez has been patiently waiting his turn. The Red Sox are used to having at least one right-handed bat on the roster who primarily gets his looks against left-handed pitchers, but Jahmai Jones has usurped that role from Gonzalez at least temporarily.
With 14 position players on the current active roster and likely 14 joining the Red Sox for the American League Wild Card Series in two weeks, there's an interesting conversation to have about Gonzalez now that the 30-year-old is having a hot month of September in Triple-A. Where will that conversation lead?
Is Gonzalez a legitimate threat to crack playoff roster?
Gonzalez batted near the top of the order for the Red Sox down the stretch last year whenever there was a lefty on the mound. But he also turned out to be battling a shoulder injury that necessitated surgery at the beginning of spring training and delayed his return to the majors until the end of June.
When he did make his season debut, Gonzalez recently admitted that he rushed his rehab, which might reasonably have thrown his swing out of whack against major league quality pitching. He went 12-for-65 with only one home run and a .572 OPS in his 19 major league games before his demotion.
“Where the team was at and all the injuries we had, it was my plan to kind of rush back and be up there,” Gonzalez said, via Christopher Smith of MassLive. “Obviously, hindsight’s 20/20.”
Now, with the Triple-A season coming to an end this weekend, Gonzalez has to know he might not make it back to the majors at all. But he's got the right attitude about the entire situation, seemingly.
“I’m ready whenever my name’s called,” Gonzalez said, per Smith.
If the Red Sox were going to put Gonzalez on the playoff roster, he'd likely have to displace either Connor Wong or Mickey Gasper. Nate Eaton, the current odd man out, should be replaced by Ceddanne Rafaela by the end of the week.

item.content:encoded:
We've reached the "wake me up for the playoffs" portion of the Boston Red Sox season.
The Red Sox have 12 games remaining on their 2026 regular-season schedule. As of Monday, they sit comfortably in the second American League Wild Card spot with a six-game lead. They're 4.5 games behind the New York Yankees in the Wild Card standings, so barring a shocking development, they'll visit the New York Yankees in the Wild Card Series for the second consecutive year.
Which 26 players will the Red Sox bring with them to the Bronx? Who's on the chopping block? Here's our 26-man playoff roster projection with 15 days until Game 1:
MORE RED SOX
Catcher (2): Adley Rutschman, Connor Wong
Cuts: None
The Red Sox could theoretically cut Wong since he'd barely see the field with Rutschman healthy. If Rutschman went down in that scenario, Mickey Gasper could go behind the plate... but that wouldn't be pretty.
Here's the problem with that approach: If Rutschman gets hurt and the Red Sox add a replacement catcher mid-series, Rutschman would be ineligible for the next playoff round. So if he got hurt in the Wild Card Series, he'd be ineligible for the ALDS and eligible to return in the ALCS.
Putting Wong on the playoff roster ensures that if Rutschman goes down, they won't need to add a mid-series replacement with Wong and Gasper already on board. And while Wong isn't exactly Pudge Rodriguez defensively, he's better than Gasper behind the dish.
Infield (7): Willson Contreras, Trevor Story, Caleb Durbin, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Nick Sogard, Mickey Gasper, Andruw Monasterio
Cuts: Curtis Mead (IL), Anthony Seigler (IL)
Even with Wong on the roster, Gasper's incredible offensive upside shown in August earns him a roster spot as a bench bat. Monasterio is on the bubble, but recent injuries may have cleared his path to a bench role.
It doesn't look like Mead (wrist) will be healthy in time for the start of the postseason.
Outfield (5): Jarren Duran, Wilyer Abreu, Ceddanne Rafaela, Roman Anthony, Jahmai Jones
Cuts: Eli White (IL), Masataka Yoshida (IL), Nate Eaton
The big question mark here is White's health, as the speedster was recently placed on the 10-day injured list with a foot ligament injury. He'll play a key bench role if healthy, but if he isn't, Jones or Eaton are the top candidates for that fifth outfield spot. We're leaning Jones because of his ability to mash left-handers.
Yoshida (hamstring) probably isn't coming back this year.
Starting rotation (3): Sonny Gray, Payton Tolle, Ranger Suarez
Cuts: Patrick Sandoval
Sandoval just hasn't been reliable, so he draws the short straw. Jake Bennett and the returning Garrett Crochet move to the bullpen -- assuming Crochet is healthy enough to give one or two quality innings in relief.
Bullpen (9): Garrett Crochet, Jake Bennett, Brayan Bello, Greg Weissert, Wyatt Olds, Erik Miller, Tyron Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock, Aroldis Chapman
Cuts: Justin Slaten (IL), Tanner Houck (IL), Johan Oviedo (IL), Alec Gamboa, Jovani Moran, Raymond Burgos
If Slaten's elbow is healthy, he's in, but it doesn't currently look like it will be since he was recently shut down from throwing.
Crochet is trending toward being ready just in time for October. So is Houck, but he hasn't pitched in a big-league game since May 2025, and he hasn't looked sharp in his rehab outings. While his upside is intriguing, we'd leave him off the initial playoff roster.
Brayan Bello makes the cut as a bulk arm after excelling in that role throughout the second half.
